pillar_reactions.evidence: Presented as the efficiency and foundation argument — 'it's the most efficient way to train... you don't have to kill yourself in the gym six days a week' and 'take into account the back surgeries, take into account the shoulders'. The prospect asked a run of mechanics questions: 'So when it comes to kettlebell weights...', 'do I need to get like one or two of each side weight', and probed his own swing technique — 'I was using a 35-pound kettlebell for that... But I know there's a way that you engage your core. Maybe I wasn't doing it right'.

Rep framed it as eating for health rather than chicken-rice-broccoli; the prospect finished the thought himself — 'You lose the weight as a side effect kind of thing' — and raised no objection despite being a certified executive chef currently running macros and meal delivery. No questions asked about it.

24/7 Trevor access, daily data entry, weekly check-ins and weekly plan adaptation were presented and tied to his own plateau — 'I know you said that you plateaued recently, went to 255 from CrossFit... we adapt the plan every week'. Prospect's only response was 'No, that sounds good.'

anchors.raw: I still have a membership at Planet Fitness. I was doing CrossFit for about eight months, and I went from 270 down to like 255
anchors.note: A gym membership plus a CrossFit box is roughly $150-250 a month in his head against $1,000 a month, and CrossFit did produce 15 lb before stalling. The rep never contrasted the two or priced the difference.

anchors.raw: I actually did the P90X with Tony Horton and that was a good workout. I mean, I saw a lot of results with that.
anchors.note: A one-off DVD purchase that he says produced real results. He ruled it out on impact tolerance, not on price or efficacy, so the low-cost-that-worked anchor stays intact.

anchors.raw: Credit cards where I used to have a six or 7% interest rate, some of them are like 24, one of them's 31%. And I don't want to pay that kind of interest.
anchors.note: The rep's default financing suggestion — 'Most people just stick it on a credit card' — collided directly with this. At 24-31% APR the effective price of the $6,000 is materially higher, and the prospect priced that himself. This is the anchor that actually stalled the deal.

anchors.raw: I started doing these, I don't know if you've heard of them, the Factor meals... and there's a local company... it's called Clean Eats
anchors.note: Already paying a premium for done-for-you meal delivery, which establishes willingness to pay for convenience in the health category. The rep spent three minutes looking the brand up rather than using it.

anchors.raw: I have a nice retirement, you know, plus, yeah, I'm old now. So I get social security too.
anchors.note: Two federal pensions, Social Security and an investment portfolio with a managing financial company. Capacity to pay is almost certainly there; it was never quantified because no financial picture was taken.

unmet_demand.want: Independent verification that the company is legitimate before sending money — he is a retired federal law-enforcement officer and said so plainly
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The only proof offered was a coaching agreement emailed by the party asking for the money, plus an invitation to research. No testimonials, client references, reviews, verifiable business details or third-party proof were provided, and the rep could not name the city his own founder lives in.

unmet_demand.want: A programme that accounts for a fused lumbar spine and NSAID-dependent shoulders — 'I'm not going to try to break it'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The mobility pillar was gestured at his surgeries but no screening, no modification framework and no clinician-liaison step exists in the offer; the guarantee actually commits to loading him 20 lb heavier on every movement in six months.

unmet_demand.want: To know what equipment to buy and what it will cost before committing
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Deferred entirely to the onboarding call — 'don't buy that until he tells you to' — leaving an unquantified equipment cost stacked on top of $6,000 at the moment of decision. He asked three times.

unmet_demand.want: To gain muscle mass, not just lose weight — 'that's, I'm not getting any muscle mass'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Probably served by the programme, but the rep positioned entirely around fat loss, efficiency and the load guarantee and never addressed hypertrophy for a former bodybuilder who cares about it specifically.
